description: Per-question search terms and relevance criteria used to pool candidate ORKG papers for the retrieval gold set. Terms are written by hand (not taken from any model's entity extraction) so the candidate pool is independent of the pipeline under test. 'titles' lists the exact titles of specific papers a lookup question asks for.

grading.2: Directly relevant: the paper's ORKG record (title or contributions) contains what the question asks for — e.g. both compared methods, the claimed result, the dataset in use, the exact paper.
grading.1: Partially relevant: on topic and useful as context, but misses part of the question (e.g. only one of two compared methods, right method but different task).
grading.0: Not relevant: lexical match only (e.g. 'A-CNN' for CNN), different topic, or no usable information.

Q01.criterion: Paper proposes, applies or studies graph neural networks.

Q03.criterion: Paper proposes or applies knowledge distillation (teacher-student).

Q04.criterion: Paper is about neural architecture search.

Q05.criterion: Paper studies contrastive / self-supervised learning of visual representations (2); contrastive learning outside vision (1).

Q06.criterion: Paper's contributions include both a CNN and an RNN (or LSTM/GRU) for text classification (2); both methods on another text task, or one method on text classification (1).

Q07.criterion: Paper reports BERT and GPT side by side on NLU tasks (2); one of them on NLU benchmarks (1).

Q08.criterion: Paper's contributions include both ResNet and VGG for image classification (2); both in another vision task, or one of them on image classification (1).

Q09.criterion: Paper compares LSTM/RNN and Transformer models on machine translation (2); one of them on MT (1).

Q10.criterion: Paper's contributions include both SVM and random forest (2); one of them as a classifier (1).

Q11.criterion: Paper trains or evaluates on ImageNet (2); uses an ImageNet variant or only ImageNet-pretrained weights (1).

Q12.criterion: Paper evaluates on SQuAD (2); question answering on another dataset (1).

Q13.criterion: Paper trains or evaluates on MNIST (2); a variant such as Fashion-MNIST (1).

Q14.criterion: Paper evaluates image models on CIFAR-10 (2); only CIFAR-100 or another CIFAR variant (1).

Q15.criterion: Paper uses CoNLL-2003 (2); NER on another CoNLL / NER dataset (1).

Q16.criterion: Paper reports BERT results on question answering compared with other / earlier methods (2); BERT on QA without comparison, or QA comparison without BERT (1).

Q17.criterion: Paper reports Transformer vs LSTM/RNN results on machine translation (2); one of them on MT with results (1).

Q18.criterion: Paper reports accuracy of both ResNet and VGG on ImageNet (2); both on another image dataset, or one of them on ImageNet with results (1).

Q19.criterion: Paper studies the effect of data augmentation on small / limited datasets (2); data augmentation in general (1).

Q20.criterion: Paper compares random forest and SVM on text classification (2); both on another task, or one of them on text classification (1).

Q21.criterion: Paper uses an attention mechanism for an NLP task (2); attention outside NLP (1).

Q22.criterion: Paper applies transfer learning to medical images (2); transfer learning in another domain, or medical imaging without transfer learning (1).

Q23.criterion: Paper uses BERT (or a BERT variant) for NER (2); BERT for another token-level task, or NER without BERT (1).

Q24.criterion: Paper uses a GAN for image generation / synthesis (2); GANs for another purpose (1).

Q25.criterion: Paper uses LSTM for sentiment analysis (2); LSTM for another text task, or sentiment analysis without LSTM (1).

Q26.criterion: The 'Attention Is All You Need' paper (Vaswani et al., 2017) (2). Lookup: only the exact paper counts.

titles: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
Q27.criterion: The original BERT paper (Devlin et al.) (2); a direct BERT follow-up such as RoBERTa (1).

titles: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
Q28.criterion: The original ResNet paper 'Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition' (2); papers proposing ResNet architecture variants (1).

titles: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space
Distributed Representations of Words and Phrases and their Compositionality
Q29.criterion: One of the original word2vec papers (Mikolov et al., 2013) (2). Lookup: only the exact paper counts.

Q30.criterion: The original GAN paper (Goodfellow et al., 2014) (2). Lookup: only the exact paper counts.

Q31.criterion: Paper does question answering on biomedical / clinical text (2); biomedical NLP that is not QA, or QA outside biomedicine (1).

Q32.criterion: Paper is about automatic speech recognition (2).

Q33.criterion: Paper builds a recommender system with deep learning (2); recommender system without deep learning (1).

Q34.criterion: Paper is about zero-shot learning (2); zero-shot evaluation of a model as a side result (1).

Q35.criterion: Paper reports both BERT and RoBERTa on GLUE (2); both on another benchmark, or one of them on GLUE (1).

Q36.criterion: Paper's contributions include both U-Net and DeepLab for segmentation (2); one of them for semantic segmentation (1).

Q37.criterion: Paper compares XGBoost / gradient boosting with deep learning, ideally on tabular data (2); XGBoost alongside other models without deep learning (1).

Q38.criterion: Paper uses MS COCO for object detection (2); COCO for another task, or object detection on another dataset (1).

Q39.criterion: Paper evaluates language models on SuperGLUE (2); only GLUE (1).

Q40.criterion: Paper uses WMT14 for machine translation (2); another WMT year or MT dataset (1).

Q41.criterion: Paper reports LSTM and GRU side by side (2); one of them with results on sequence modeling (1).

Q42.criterion: Paper reports GNN results on node classification, ideally against non-graph baselines (2); GNN on another graph task (1).

Q43.criterion: Paper reports YOLO and Faster R-CNN side by side (as method/baseline) with speed or accuracy (2); both mentioned without results, or one of them in real-time detection (1).

Q44.criterion: Paper applies CNNs to medical image analysis (2); CNNs on non-medical images, or medical imaging without CNNs (1).

Q45.criterion: Paper uses a VAE for representation learning (2); VAE used for generation or another purpose (1).

Q46.criterion: Paper uses random forest for feature selection / importance (2); random forest only as a classifier (1).

Q47.criterion: Paper uses word2vec embeddings for sentiment analysis (2); word2vec for another task, or sentiment analysis with other embeddings (1).

Q48.criterion: The ELMo paper 'Deep contextualized word representations' (Peters et al., 2018) (2). Lookup: only the exact paper counts.

titles: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
Q49.criterion: The original ViT paper (2); papers proposing ViT variants for image recognition (1).

terms: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning
titles: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
Q50.criterion: The T5 paper 'Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer' (Raffel et al.) (2). Lookup: only the exact paper counts.
